§6Technetium-99§f

§aThe first fission product you'll actually care about. Mildly radioactive, extremely useful.§f

§bTechnetium-99§f is a common byproduct of uranium and plutonium fission. At §e2.75 RAD/s§f, it's the tamest thing coming out of your reactor. You'll want a lot of it.

§6Where It Comes From§f:
§b•§f §bDepleted ZIRNOX Fuel§f, process spent uranium, plutonium, or MOX rods
§b•§f §bDepleted Research Reactor Fuel§f, same deal
§b•§f §bU-235 Short-Lived Waste§f, Tc-99 makes up §e20%§f of the U-235 type

§6What It's For§f:
§b•§f §bTechnetium Steel§f, the corrosion-resistant alloy you'll use everywhere
§b•§f §bSelf-Charging Batteries§f, low-output perpetual power

Every uranium-based fuel except natural uranium, MOX, and plutonium yields Tc-99 when reprocessed. Start with ZIRNOX spent fuel, it's the lowest-effort source.

§ePS:§f Check JEI for which fuels produce technetium. The research reactor fuels are richer sources but more expensive to run.
